title: Grass-silage 90-day fermentation, press-juice chemistry, and press-cake methane-potential reference observations
citation: Steinbrenner, J., Mueller, J., & Oechsner, H. (2022). Combined Butyric Acid and Methane Production from Grass Silage in a Novel Green Biorefinery Concept. Waste and Biomass Valorization, 13, 1873–1884. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12649-021-01626-4
source_locations: Results section, methane-yield paragraph and Figure 3, printed p.1881
geography: Unterer Lindenhof, Eningen unter Achalm, Germany
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), as stated by the publisher; attribution and license link retained.
material_scope: Intensively managed agricultural grass harvested on 2018-05-23, chopped to 8 mm, and ensiled in small jars. The grassland was cut up to four times per year and fertilized with digestate. This is cultivated grass silage, not roadside grass, VARTA feed, or a protein-depleted GreenHub residual.
experimental_conditions: Eight treatments: untreated control (C), water addition (W), CaCO3 addition (B), and combined water plus CaCO3 (WB), each held at 22 ± 1 °C or 37 ± 1 °C. Jars were opened after 3, 14, 30, and 90 days; endpoint composition is transcribed for day 90 only. Table 3 concentrations are reported per kg total solids; Table 4 press-juice concentrations are per kg fresh matter. Pressing used a tincture press at 20 MPa for 60 s. Press-cake methane potential used triplicate Hohenheim Biogas Yield Tests at 37 °C for 35 days, normalized to 273.15 K and 1013 hPa.
data_scope: 147 records: 80 Table 3 endpoint silage measurements, 64 Table 4 press-juice measurements, and 3 explicitly quantified press-cake specific methane yields stated in the Results text. The Tables 3–4 means and SDs are preserved separately. Censored <0.1 results remain text, not zero. Numeric methane yields not stated in the article text are blank rather than digitized from a figure.
limitations: Reference-only; none of these observations are GreenHub defaults, runtime parameters, or evidence of a validated storage kinetic model.
The study uses cultivated German grass under controlled jar ensiling, not roadside grass, commercial storage piles, or the GreenHub feed basis.
Only the 90-day treatment endpoints are transcribed; do not interpolate the 3-, 14-, and 30-day time points or fit rate constants from these endpoints.
VS loss is an endpoint under the study treatments and cannot be interpreted as mass loss without the corresponding initial and final inventories.
Table 4 press-juice COD is reported as g/kg fresh matter; it must not be reinterpreted as mg/L or mapped directly to GreenHub brown-juice COD.
The three numeric methane-yield values included were stated in the Results text. The remaining treatment values shown only graphically were not digitized.
conversion_or_processing: Published means, SDs, units, treatment labels, replicate count, bases, and censored observations were transcribed. The paper's m3 CH4/kg VS was normalized in the article to standard temperature/pressure; the CSV labels this as Nm3 CH4/kg VS without additional numeric conversion. No interpolation, figure digitization, imputation, or kinetic fitting was performed.
uncertainty: Table means and SDs are published for triplicate experiments. Raw replicate-level data are not included in the article; the authors state collected data can be provided on request.
